stem: An employee receives a phone call from someone claiming to be from the IT service desk, asking them to read out the code that just arrived on their phone. What is this?

options.why: The channel is a voice call, which makes it vishing, and the goal is to defeat the second factor.
Technically part of the phishing family, and the exam wants the channel specific term when the channel is stated.
Smishing arrives by SMS. The code arrived by SMS, the attack arrived by phone call.
Whaling targets an executive. Nothing indicates the employee is one.

stem: Finance receives an email from the CFO's genuine mailbox, in their usual style, asking for an urgent wire transfer to a new account. Mail authentication passes because the message really did come from that mailbox. What is this?

options.why: The attacker controls a real, legitimate mailbox, which is why SPF, DKIM and DMARC all pass and the message reads as authentic.
Whaling targets an executive. Here the executive's account is the weapon, and finance staff are the target.
Nothing is spoofed. The message genuinely originates from the CFO's account, which is what makes it so effective.
The channel is email, not SMS.

stem: An attacker compromises a managed service provider and uses its remote management tooling to deploy ransomware to 200 of its clients simultaneously. Which risk does this illustrate?

options.text: Third-party and supply chain risk through a service provider's privileged access
options.why: The MSP holds trusted administrative access into every client, so compromising it once reaches all of them.

options.text: Insider threat at each of the 200 clients
options.why: No client employee acted. The trusted access came from outside each organisation.
The MSP relationship is sanctioned and contracted, which is the opposite of shadow IT.

options.text: A zero-day in the clients' endpoint protection
options.why: The deployment used legitimate management tooling with legitimate credentials, so no exploit was needed.

stem: Staff at an engineering firm are compromised after visiting a small industry standards site they all read daily. The site itself was breached a week earlier and now serves a malicious script to visitors from that firm's address range. Which threat vector is this?

options.why: The attacker compromised a site the target population is already known to visit, then waited. No message was sent to anyone.
Typosquatting registers a lookalike domain and relies on a mistyped address. Here the victims reached exactly the site they meant to visit.
Brand impersonation forges the appearance of a trusted organisation. The site here was genuine and genuinely compromised, which is why nothing looked wrong.
BEC runs through a real or spoofed mailbox to push a transaction. No email was involved in this chain.

stem: A vulnerability review finds a reporting service reachable on the network whose web console still accepts the vendor's shipped administrator password. No user interaction is needed to exploit it. Which description fits the vector best?

options.text: An open service port exposing software with default credentials
options.why: The opening is the exposed service plus an unchanged shipped credential. It is reached directly, with nobody tricked into anything.

options.text: A message-based vector, because the console is reached over the web
options.why: Message-based means a human is addressed and asked to act: email, SMS, instant message, voice call. Browsing to a service is not that.

options.text: A supply chain vector, because the vendor shipped the password
options.why: Supply chain means the attacker uses trust you extended to a supplier. Here the vendor's default is simply a configuration you failed to change on your own estate.

options.text: A zero-day, because no patch has been applied
options.why: Nothing is unknown to the vendor here and no patch is missing. A password that was never changed is a hardening failure, not a vulnerability awaiting a fix.

stem: During a product recall, coordinated accounts post fabricated claims that a company's safety certificates were withdrawn. Share price falls and the support desk is overwhelmed. Nothing on the company network is touched. Which best describes what is being used against the company?

options.why: The objectives list this as a human vector in its own right. The asset under attack is trust, and no system has to be breached to damage it.
Brand impersonation means posing as the company. These accounts are speaking about the company, not pretending to be it.
The support desk is overwhelmed by real people reacting to a story. No traffic is being directed at a service to exhaust it.
Pretexting builds a false scenario to extract something from a specific target. This is broadcast, and it asks nobody for anything.
